text_fidelity_a:
Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

The packaging indicated Callie is from Japan, and she definitely has more almond-shaped eyes than Meredith. Her light skin, brown hair (instead of black), and eye shape reminded my bi-racial girls of themselves. That is the true gift of doll lines that have unique face sculpts, to provide a mirror so all little girls can have a doll that resembles them, as well as a truly diverse line of dolls.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie

text_fidelity_a:
SmartLab Toys That's Gross Science Lab this is still a good starter book on a difficult but important topic.
Science is a great subject that all need to learn better and That’s Gross Science Lab attempts to bring the fun of learning to curious kids. It encourages kids to conduct science experiments, each with an emphasis on learning and on creating something, well, gross and disgusting.

My girls love the subject of science and they did like this science set when it was introduced to them for the first time. I was a little disappointed when I opened the box and found it contained so little. You get three molds- one for barf, one for a centipede, and one for a maggot; a toilet mixer; a plastic jar; a bubble wand; spoon; two beakers and a stand. A small booklet with experiment ideas gets kids and parents started so they can create and laugh at so many gross things.

With the experiments, there are a total of 20 and some of them are fun for kids. But one problem I have is that every single one of them requires household ingredients, which you may or may not have. We were still able to do some of them right away because all they required was baking soda, corn starch, eggs, etc. But others required a special visit to the store and this could be upsetting to children and parents who want to open the box and start experimenting immediately.

What you get with this science kit isn’t much, but I must admit that it does get kids interested in science even more than before. In fact, that might be the most compelling reason to buy this science kit. It helps pique kids’ interests and makes them want to investigate more about the world around them. Other than that, this is a toy of average worth that may or may not satisfy those who buy it.
text_fidelity_b: SmartLab Toys That's Gross Science Lab

text_fidelity_a:
Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+ This game hits that sweet spot where the complexity is enough for adults but not so high that kids struggle. And it’s FUN! It says 9 and up but my 7-year-old caught on pretty quickly and was delighted when we talked about it in terms of executing a program. My family loves this game. My husband and I can see playing it with just adults too.

The gameplay involves drafting cards and then using them to create a plan for how the mole will move on the grid, which is essentially a simple program much like one would write on a computer. It takes some strategy, but you can only predict other people so much and this is where the game shines.

I was worried it would be too complex or long when we read the rules, but it plays very smoothly! We felt comfortable within 2 rounds, and it was a lot of fun seeing how the plans we made would be thwarted as other players move. We also enjoyed how the turn order changed. There are many levels of subtle strategy, I feel like we will be learning new things each time we play. There is a random element of dice when placing a rock on the board, simple but genius game design. It keeps it from feeling unfair, and adds an element of luck to using it.

Even when you are losing, it’s so interesting to see the programs unfold as each card flips that it didn’t feel upsetting, and most of the points are earned in the later rounds as the mounds get higher so you can easily catch back up to an early lead or after a bad round. This means you don’t feel too discouraged if you have a poor start.

I like that it has a defined timeline, there are 6 rounds and you know what they will look like. Overall a great choice for a family game night as it is not likely to overrun an hour.

The double-layer boards and gameplay are unique and the story of the moles is full of flavor. The art is charming and the explanation of the rules such as “moles are too polite so they don’t move when they hit another” is a really sweet touch. The printing is great quality, the game is just beautiful to look at. The box is well-organized making setup and takedown easy, and it looks pretty on the shelf. Plus, we love the moles! The standees make great pieces. This game shows a lot of care in the details, and we love games with a lot of artistic flavor.

We play a lot of games as a family, but when we finished this one kiddo said this was their new favorite! The only downside is the limit of 2-4 players–it keeps it moving but means we can’t invite more friends to play at a time!

Bonus, the box art is beautiful so this also would make a lovely gift to open.
text_fidelity_b: Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+

And I have a love/hate relationship with the uploading option. I have to manually hook it up to my computer via usb cord to upload to the internet. On one hand, this feels "old school" and is time consuming... but on the other, at least I can monitor and limit everything my kids want to upload to their (locked and private) youtube channel. If my daughter had her way, upload two dozen videos a day!
Anyway, I can't recommend this toy video camera enough. I'm certain any child that has expressed interest in creating their own youtube videos will LOVE this! It really is that awesome. Thank you VTech!!!

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Wooden Stamp Set: Vehicles - 10 Stamps, 5 Colored Pencils, 2-Color Stamp Pad Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is a fun toy that encourages creativity and keeps kids occupied. This stamp kit comes complete with nine different stamps, a small ink pad with pink and purple ink, and five colored pencils for your child's creative enjoyment.

Melissa and Doug toys are known for education, creativity, and durability and most every product the company makes can be counted on to posses at least two of these qualities. The same is true with this toy. The Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set isn't big on educational quality, but it does encourage creativity and the set and storage container are made from wood, for better durability. The wooden container offers easy storage so that pieces do not get lost and the product's individual pieces are designed to last.

Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is simple yet fun and requires little supervision or explaining. My little princesses like this toy and still find it fun, but I have noticed that it lacks the staying power of some of their favorite toys. Unless I suggest it, they are not likely to use it. They do like it, but I think they have become a little bored with it. They prefer toys with movement and sound, and this offers neither.

This stamp set is certainly durable, but one thing that isn't made to last is the ink pad. I like that the Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set comes complete with its own ink and my girls strongly appreciate that the ink is colored purple and pink. However, don't expect the ink to last very long. The small blotches of ink will not offer many stamping adventures, so be prepared to purchase additional ink stamps within a few months.

Although not the perfect toy, the Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is nonetheless a good toy for little princesses everywhere. It has many positive qualities, encourages creativity, and is priced right. Like I said, it lacks staying power, but it has enough positive qualities to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Wooden Stamp Set: Vehicles - 10 Stamps, 5 Colored Pencils, 2-Color Stamp Pad

Disney Sorcerer's Arena: Epic Alliances Core Set | Strategy Board Game for 2 or 4 Players Ages 13 & Up | Featuring Disney and Pixar Characters & Villains | Officially-Licensed Family Game If there was one company I can confidently say I wouldn't have expected a skirmish miniature battle game to come from, it would be a Disney mashup. Ariel and Aladdin get out there and trade punches with Gaston? I wouldn't have thought.

But that's exactly what you have here. The character mashup is novel, and the board, pieces and cards are pretty good quality, although I am not a fan of the poorly implemented version of the "Heroclix" format you see on these acrylic minis. They look good, they're just a bit difficult to fiddle with.

The game is broken into chapters, and you can really start exploring the entire set starting with Chapter 2 rules, which are a good starting point for experienced gamers and older children as well.

I'm excited to see what could come from the expansions for this game and which characters they choose to add. I don't think there are going to be a lot of people who gravitate towards Dr. Facilier, for example, so some more fan favorites would be nice to see.

Generally speaking, I really like this game and I think it will make for a fun tactical combat game for people of any age to enjoy.

text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games Werewords Deluxe Edition I very much liked the original edition of Werewords (essentially the same game as Insider), and this is the same game, but there's more of it.

Werewords is a lot like "20 questions". Players ask yes/no questions in an attempt to identify a word that could be anything from "spatula" to "Mjollnir". One player is a werewolf, who knows the word already, and is attempting to guide the players with their questioning closer to the actual word without them figuring out that they know the word already. They win if players can identify the word, but do not know which among them is the werewolf. If they do identify the werewolf, then the werewolf can also identify the "seer" player (another with information about the word).

The deluxe edition contains a few additional roles for players. If you already have the other version of this game, I don't think you need to own this version unless you're a completionist. If you don't own any versions of this game, I think it's quite good.

My concern remains the same as before - the app for this game is good, and it doesn't appear to be going anywhere, but if you don't want to run an app while playing this game, then I totally understand, and this game will not be for you at all. I think the app does a good job of balancing the words against one another, creating the ability to discern easy from very difficult words, but the same effect could have been accomplished with cards. I would prefer the cards as well, but the app has the advantage of saving shelf space and also having a larger directory of words. In the end, it's a toss up, but if you don't mind the app, then this is the best possible edition of the game to get.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Werewords Deluxe Edition

text_fidelity_a:
Wonder Forge Marvel I Can Do That! Game We also have this game in the Dr. Seuss theme, and they're both fun. They're very similar in both cards and directions, but this one is great for little fans of Marvel.

There's a note on the directions page to let you know it's fine to customize the rules for your family. (We tend to do that anyway, but it's a great reminder!) There are 3 stacks of numbered/colored cards(1-red, 2-blue, 3-green). The player turns over one card from each stack. They'll tell the player what to do with which objects. For example, the first card will tell you to "Do a push-up". The second card: "with Captain Marvel's energy ball", and the third card: "on your head". Some tasks are harder than others! Each card will get a certain amount of stars. (At the end of the game, the players will add the stars up. The player with the most wins.) If your child thinks he/she can do the specified task, they will say, "I Can Do That!" If not, they can exchange a card at a time until they feel they can do the task. One of my children was given the task of "Crab walk under the portal, with Spider-Man's web, between your elbows". None of us were talented enough to do that, so he picked again. This is also a great escape route for the shyer(or younger) little ones. Some things will be less embarrassing or more doable for them than others.

There are also "Battle" cards. If one of those are drawn, then any other cards drawn will be put back in the mix. The player will then try to knock down the Green Goblin card with the object specified on the card. If the task is completed, the card is set aside. If not, the player has to put that card in his/her pile as a reminder to discard 2 cards before counting stars at the end of the game. (That way, they can discard to 2 with the lowest number of stars.)

While it may get old with what the players do, it does create a variety of mix and match tasks. The cards are constantly being shuffled. The game ends when all the cards are gone.

This is a great game for when movement is needed. It's not one that the players just sit around and play. The players have to get up and move around. There's also a nice variety of types of objects. There's a plastic block that will need to be filled with air, along with a ball(that's already aired up). There's foam items and thick cardboard objects(Green Goblin and Captain America's shield). My biggest complaint is the "portal". This isn't the sturdiest of things. It's hard to get it to stand up straight, mainly because it has to be rolled up a bit to fit in the box. It makes it hard to get under at times. The bigger/older the child, the harder it will be to crawl under it, either way. This is definitely a game for littler/younger people. Also, I fear that the block won't last long, since objects that require air don't make it too long around my home, in general. (For it to fit back in the box after each game, the air will have to be released. That means you'll have to blow it up before each game. It's not huge, so it's not the biggest deal. Particularly if used in a classroom setting, though, germs/cleaning wipes would be something to put into consideration.)

My children(3, 5, and a tiny 8) have really enjoyed playing this game, though!
text_fidelity_b: Wonder Forge Marvel I Can Do That! Game

The only thing I don't like about this set is the silly names applied to the colors. I get that it is supposed to be cute but does the black color really need to be called 'little black dress' and 'twilight sky' instead of blue. I totally get why crayola does this for their crayons where there are hundreds of colors with similar shades that need unique names.. but it makes no sense to apply silly names to basic black and blue colors, and especially to use several different names for the same color (ie the black shade is 'little black dress' for dry-erase markers but the black permanent marker is 'always onyx').

My 6 year old daughter was reading the dry-erase marker and was quite confused why it said 'little black dress' when it is a marker and not a dress.. Baby Alive Beautiful Now Baby Doll This is a very cute doll that any little girl (and perhaps some boys) would adore.
Even adults who are into collecting dolls might be interested, although I would not call this a collector doll by any means. It is a doll that is meant to be played with. The pretend scissors look pretty safe and do move back and forth and make a clicking sound. The water squirt bottle might be okay for some kids, but I know some kids would be using it to squirt someone with, instead of the doll's hair, so use your own judgment on that. At least it only holds a few ounces of water or whatever you put in it. Some kids I know would probably put soda in it and be squirting it into their mouths! The doll does have a really full head of hair, so those children who enjoy it, will probably have fun combing the hair and styling it and using one of 3 barrettes. Educational value for grooming?--maybe a little, but this is not an educational toy. The dress the doll wears is cute, with a pink poodle on it. I really don't think you can go wrong with this doll as a gift for young children who like dolls, even if they don't care that much about the grooming aspect. The eyes are painted on and don't look realistic to me, but at least nothing that can be broken or poked out. The doll's skin is slightly brown and the box has Spanish wording as well as English, so could be appropriate for children of varying skin tones.
text_fidelity_b: Baby Alive Beautiful Now Baby Doll

This game plays identically to regular Uno in almost every way. It has all of the expected elements of the game - 4 colors, skip, reverse, wild cards and more. However, it also has a special card that changes the game in a fun and often unexpected way, allowing a player to dodge attack cards and send them back to the one who played them. It's powerful enough to change gameplay but not enough to ruin the game.

The cards are decorated with the familiar characters of Mario Brothers games - Bowser, Mario, Luigi, Donkey Kong Jr. and more. Fans of the Mario Brothers franchise will like this deck.

The game is packed nicely in a metal tin that protects the cards and keeps them together.

I am not the least bit unhappy with this game and my family and I have been enjoying it. We look forward to game nights and this game will be a part of those nights.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games ​Mattel Games PIC FLIP Card Matching Game with 110 Cards in a Decorative Tin, Makes a Great Gift for 7 Year Olds and Up [Amazon Exclusive]

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Glow Book Seeing commercials for the Glow Book, I've been interested in this toy for my 9 year old. Obviously commercials are made to show the absolute best of a product, so I expected it to be much less than what was advertised. I have to admit it's almost as cool as the advertisements. However, the best way to discover if a toy is really worth it is to test it out on more than just a few kids. I went with those who were interested in art. Thus, this is judging based on kids who are already fans of art.

Honest opinions from kids:

1. It came with pages you could trace for kids who can't draw too well.
2. If you make a mistake, it's easy to erase it, but it's hard to make it all clean. You really have to rub well to erase mistakes or it leaves smearing behind. They should have something to erase it better. At least you can use it more than one time.
3. It needs more pages. You have plastic pages you draw on and the lights come on to show each page. It makes everything look like it's moving when the lights flash. The pages also aren't very straight.
4. I really like to play with the glow book because it is fun. You just have to get used to using it.
5. It was just like a movie. I could color and draw it just how I pleased.
6. It would be nice if there could be just a little more colors because it shows purple in some of the tracings, but there is no purple. Maybe some black to show outlines, too. It just comes with six colors: tan, pink, yellow, blue, red and green.

From an adult's perspective - it definitely has keep the interest going with the kids. It's not a toy that ends up on the shelf - lost and forgotten. However, the price tag is a bit high for something that's so simple. I have seen Amazon have excellent deals on the Glow Book, however, and think if you are patient and give yourself time to find a great deal, you will. Anything less than $20 would be great. I agree with one of the children that it could use more colors. Especially when dealing with kids interested in art. For younger kids, the small amount of color choices is probably fine. Glass cleaner takes care of the smudges you'll find after repeated use by kids. After a few mistakes, the drawing takes on a foggy/dusty look - thus making it harder to see the pictures "move" clearly. Downside is it can't be cleaned until the child is entirely finished. Definitely stick with the manufacturer age recommendation of 6 years and up. This toy is not made well enough to handle rough use from younger kids.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Glow Book

text_fidelity_a:
ADORA Baby Doll Stroller with Color Changing Sunny Days Print, Fits Up to 18 Inch Baby Dolls 3 stars

This stroller is very cute, and it is nice that it is in gender-neutral colors, so that boy children as well as girl children can enjoy this stroller. It can be used not just to hold baby dolls, but also stuffed animals.

This toy stroller resembles a typical human-baby, umbrella stroller in design and functionality. The difference between this and a real stroller, though, other than the miniature sizing, is that it is not sturdy. Therefore, there is a safety element in that your child may easily push or lean harder on its handles than it is built to withstand, and end up tripping and falling on top of or tumbling headfirst over it. If you have stairs in your house, this in particular could lead to a dangerous injury.

A major factor contributing to this flimsiness issue is the fact that the wheels are not at all strong and, overall, this toy is very cheaply made. It is certainly not constructed to stand up to the rather rugged treatment a toddler or preschooler would give to a toy like this.

In short, this doll stroller is certainly not a case of, "You get what you pay for." Because of the expensive price of this and all other Adora doll accessories, you'd think you'd be getting something really sturdy and long-lasting. Unfortunately, that is not the case with this stroller.
text_fidelity_b: ADORA Baby Doll Stroller with Color Changing Sunny Days Print, Fits Up to 18 Inch Baby Dolls

LEGO City Service Station 60257 Pretend Play Toy, Building Sets for Kids, New 2020 (354 Pieces) This LEGO CITY SERVICE STATION 60257 BUILDING SET (New 2020; 354 Pieces) is intended for kids aged 5 years and up, so it’s simple to build. Of course, that means there isn’t a lot of fine detail in the vehicles and buildings, despite the high piece count. Many of the 354 pieces are small ones, like single round studs for headlights, or a puppy figure, or a hot dog.

Still, this is a rather cool service station, because it includes a charging station for an electric SUV, in addition to gas pumps for a more traditional van. The set includes a mini-convenience store/pay station. The van opens up to show a spacious interior. Both vehicles can accommodate a minifig in the driver’s seat. text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) I'm just combining my thoughts on the various guns and products into one review, in case anyone would like to do a bit of comparing in one spot.

Darts:

The darts are kind of like a third of a straw, with a cool rubber-like tip. These tips ONLY stick to the special targets, which are on the shields(both the wearable ones and the ones that attach to the guns). There are also targets that stick to the wall. (I just taped the top of these targets, as opposed to sticking the whole thing on the wall.) We tested these out on mirrors and windows. They really don't stick to anything, but the special targets.

They're mostly bright colored, which makes it easier to find them once they've been shot. You'll have to take several time outs just to gather darts.

This company has made it perfectly clear that these darts are NOT made for little ones. I just want to reinforce that. I have an 18 month old that puts things in his mouth constantly. We found a large rock in his poo diaper. :S These are simply irresistible to him with their chewy rubber tip. He's chewed the tops off a few of them, even when we were trying to keep a close eye on him. The tops DO come off when chewed on, so these are definitely a choking hazard for little ones.

I try to teach our boys to never aim a gun at anyone, but I've been hit with a few of the darts. One hurt, but the others didn't. I think it depends on how close the gun is, and simply how the dart hits a person. In general, they don't seem to hurt too much.

Other than chewing, they seem pretty sturdy, though. They're had lots of use and bending, but they still work in the guns.

Farshot Blaster:

This is the smallest gun in this line(that we have...there seems to be a smaller "clipfire"). You pull back the top to "pump it up". It will only hold 1 dart at a time for shooting, but 2 spares fit in the bottom of the gun.

This gun is the easiest to aim, as far as target practice, and if that's what you'd like it for, I'd recommend this one. I've found it to be a great stress reliever. When the little ones are creating chaos, I can pull out this gun, tape a target to the wall, and do a little target practice.

Twisted Spinner Blaster:

This is the medium sized gun in this line. To shoot it, you pull an arm on the gun back towards yourself. The darts are loaded in the round end. It will hold 8 darts. As with all the guns, it comes with removable shields.

This one is a little harder to aim, but it's still fun.

Rapid Madness Blaster:

This is the largest gun in this line. You push and pull an arm to pump it up. The trigger is super sensitive, so it takes a couple of seconds to shoot all 20 darts that it holds. Those darts are held in a clip that slides into the side of the gun. This one is the most fun, BUT you don't get much shooting time before having to round up darts.

Bandolier:

This is an adjustable strap that you can wear across your body. It has a special target that the darts will stick to. It will also hold 12 extra darts.

Eye goggles:

These are pretty cool. As advertised, they won't fog up. They're made of a thick-like plastic/rubber, and give you "bug vision". They're also adjustable. My little ones are younger than the recommended age, but the clip kept coming off with them, and we put the goggles back together so much that I wanted to throw them away. Still, I don't think adults will have that problem, and they really are pretty cool!

Targets:

These are a little smaller than I prefer, but they do come in slightly different sizes and shapes. You get different points for different areas. The darts DO stick really well to these targets, and ONLY these targets, but if the dart hits wrong, it still won't stick. I'd say our darts stuck about half the time with the larger guns, and about 3/4th of the time with the farshot blaster. You can peel the back off and it will stick to the wall/door, but as I mentioned above, I just taped it instead. They're a fun way to create a little "battle" zone in one's room, or just simple target practice.

Overall, we've had tons of fun with these guns, and just think they're all pretty awesome.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

Selfie - The Game of Silly Expressions Well first I have to admit, I do not have an internet saavy family. And this game is very much tied into internet memes from "I can haz cheezburgers?" to "Erhmahgerd." Luckily, I have spent a healthy amount of my life researching internet culture, but I ended up having to explain a lot of the cards to my kids.

But the reason I love this game is because of how engaged it kept the kids, and the amount of laughs that it produced. The selfies were ridiculous and caused laughter in itself and the cards played were even better. The game is pretty simple, pick a card from your hand to recreate in a selfie, then others play cards with scenarios that best fit your selfie. There are a lot of "Trying not to poop" type of cards so the humor is a little juvenile but perfect for keeping kids engaged.

Everyone willingly took their turns on the cell phone and everyone seemed to really enjoy the game. Scoring was pretty meaningless which was good. I was thinking that since the person taking the photo got to be the judge of who gets the point for the best caption that there would be hurt feelings and poorly awarded points, but the fun of the selfies and reading the cards trumped any controversy. Actually we ended without caring who scored points.

All in all this is a great ice breaking game.
text_fidelity_b: Selfie - The Game of Silly Expressions

Giant Clue Classic Mystery Party Retro Board Game Summer Toy with Large Rooms, Giant Cards, and Foam Tools, for Kids and Families Ages 8 and up We tried this recently on a rainy evening, and it was a fun family activity. However it feels like some things weren't fully thought through and could have been easily made better.
For example, the spinner needle feels like it stops exactly on the line more than half the time, causing much arguing and debate over which side it actually landed. If you have ever played the game Life or used a spinning prize wheel, you know there is a much better way to do this: Have plastic borders that catch on the needle so it stops in one space clearly (and makes a cool motor noise as it click-click-clicks quickly). Once you're making giant playing pieces and a large floor mat board, this would not have added a lot of cost and would have made the game infinitely more fun and smooth to play.
And speaking of giant playing pieces, once you assemble them, they don't fit back in the box unless you break them apart, something that probably won't last if you do it every time you put the game away. It could have come with a bag or something to store the game board and pieces in. As of now, I'm pretty sure the pieces and board are going to get separated from each other in our family room. It's a fun game, but unlike giant versions of Jenga, Connect Four or Chess, the novelty of giant Sorry wears off quickly and at some point my mother-in-law actually asked why we can't just play it on the table like a regular game. It's fun for the novelty, but the caveats and game mechanics make this not worth more than 3 stars in my opinion.
text_fidelity_b: Giant Clue Classic Mystery Party Retro Board Game Summer Toy with Large Rooms, Giant Cards, and Foam Tools, for Kids and Families Ages 8 and up

Klutz Sun Catchers Craft Kit I thought this would be a cool activity to do with my 6 year old. She LOVES crafts, and I actually bought a coloring "stained glass" art book by Klutz for her in the past (which she loved)
It was a little hard to tell exactly what the process was of making them just by looking at the pictures, and It was actually a bit more difficult than I assumed.

So you take the colored film paper, trace the shape out of the book, cut it out, then place it on the sticky paper to puzzle all the colored pieces together like a mosaic, to make up the whole picture. You youths choose to do them any color you want, but the more colors you use to make up the picture, the more patience and precision you will need.
We started off simple with the strawberry (only 2 colors) which was pretty easy.
I went to apply the puff paint and it would not come out of the top of the tube. I tried to cut the nozzle down, squeeze it out slow which ended in it coming out the side of the bottle, and getting all over my fingers. It was so thick, I assumed it got semi dried out, so I threw it away to prevent any further mess.
Since we were unable to use the puff paint, my daughter outlined the strawberry with black sharpie. Unfortunately without the puff paint, the film paper is pretty flimsy.
Even though we did not get the full effect of the project, we still had some fun doing the craft together.
text_fidelity_b: Klutz Sun Catchers Craft Kit

text_fidelity_a:
dreambuilderToy Building Bricks 1100 Pieces Set with All Popular Building Blocks The theme for my five-year old's birthday party was Lego Batman. Therefore, I needed a bunch of Lego bricks to make decorations, but I did not want to pay an expensive Lego price and I also just needed basic bricks and colors. Enter the Dreambuilder Toy Building Bricks with 1000 bricks! Not only did I get exactly what I wanted, but I also got a superior toy. I was able to "build" all the decorations I needed (a napkin and silverware holder) with lots of bricks to spare, but when the party was over, I gave my son all the bricks and he was none the wiser that these were not "real" Legos. Some of the older boys at the party inspected the decorations and were able to come to a conclusion that these were in fact not real Legos, but that does not matter because they function exactly like real Legos.

Within the bag you get basic bricks in various sizes, 1x1, 2x2, 2x6, 2x8, etc. There is also one small, green building plate. The set also comes with various bricks for roofs, doors, fences, and windows. The colors are Roy G. Biv with black, white, and grey added. There are equal amounts of each color. We do have a real Lego 1000 piece "creative" bucket and here are the differences. There is no idea booklet with this. However, I do believe you can check their website for building ideas. Therefore, if free form building is not for your child like it is for mine, then this set is not for you. There is no brick separator, and the really flat bricks that drove us adults insane when we were kids are back to haunt to us. You will need to purchase one separately unlike the Lego creative sets. The Lego creative sets have more unique bricks, which take away from having more basic bricks to build bigger and better things as you would with this set. Dreambuilder bricks do not come with a storage bucket. You will receive a plastic bag with all of the bricks contained within that bag. So, you will need your own storage box.

Overall, I find the Dreambuilder bricks to be vastly superior to Lego if you are into simple, old school, free building without instructions. I will be purchasing additional sets.
text_fidelity_b: dreambuilderToy Building Bricks 1100 Pieces Set with All Popular Building Blocks

text_fidelity_a:
Thomas & Friends Construction Engine, 3 Pack Pros.

They ran on our carpet, and on a Melissa and Doug train track. They couldn’t wait to get home to run them on the Fisher Price Thomas track.

You do need six triple aaa batteries. Two for each engine. None are provided.
You must remove a very small screw on the opposite side of the coupling.
After installing the batteries, I didn’t see any start lever, and thought I had a defective engine.
On inspection, after installing the batteries, you need to make certain the start lever is sticking out of the slit on the top of the engine, before tightening the screw back. I tightened it without being aware of this, and although the screw did tighten, the lever was in the wrong spot.

This is a very attractive set of engines and will get a lot of use.
text_fidelity_b: Thomas & Friends Construction Engine, 3 Pack
